title: Serene Sunrise WALK in an English Village with Thatched Roof Cottages | Birdsong - ENGLAND
description:
Experience the timeless beauty and historical depth of West Overton, an English village in Wiltshire, England. Enjoy this tranquil walk with natural sounds, spring flowers in full bloom, birdsongs, and thatched cottages.

West Overton is rich in history and charm, making it a perfect destination for nature lovers and history enthusiasts.

St John’s Church: Built in 1877-8, this beautiful church is a cornerstone of the village’s heritage.

Walk with me to discover the village's Bronze Age, Roman, and later historical settlements.

There were 37 poll-tax payers recorded in West Overton in 1377 and the population in 1801 was 172 residents.

Many 18th-century roads and lanes were still visible as tracks in 1977.

Overton Manor House: A stunning 16th and 17th-century manor house near the church, featuring a tile-hung upper floor and a red brick former barn.

Much of the village was rebuilt in the 1870s with gabled cottages designed by the renowned architect Mr. Ponting, who lived in nearby Lockeridge.

title: This is Spring in the Cotswolds | A Calm Early Morning Walk
description:
Join me for a calm early morning walk through Lower Dowdeswell in the Cotswolds, as the first signs of spring begin to appear. The light is soft and the air feels fresh.

This walk captures that quiet moment early in the season, birds becoming more active, new growth starting to show and the gentle shift from winter into spring. The lanes, fields and stone cottages sit quietly in the morning light, with just the natural sounds of the countryside.

There’s no talking or music, just birdsong, light movement in the landscape and the calm atmosphere of an early spring morning.

ABOUT LOWER DOWDESWELL

Lower Dowdeswell is a small village in Gloucestershire, set within the Cotswolds Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty near Cheltenham. The village lies in the Dowdeswell Valley, surrounded by open fields and gently rolling countryside.

The name “Dowdeswell” is thought to come from Old English, meaning a spring or stream belonging to a person named Dudda, reflecting the natural water features in the area. The village has medieval origins and developed as a farming community, shaped by agriculture and sheep grazing that supported the Cotswolds’ historic wool trade.

At the centre of the village stands the church of St Michael and All Angels, with parts dating back to the Norman period. The surrounding cottages and buildings are made from traditional Cotswold stone and reflect centuries of rural life.

In early spring, the area begins to change, hedgerows start to fill out, birds return, and the countryside slowly shifts into a new season while still holding onto its quiet character.

title: Autumn Colours in an English Village – Peaceful Countryside Walk, England
description:
NEW WALK: Kelmscott, Oxfordshire – Autumn Colours

Experience the beauty of **Kelmscott**, one of Oxfordshire’s most picturesque riverside villages, during the golden glow of autumn. As the leaves turn and fall, I take you on a calm morning walk through quiet lanes, historic cottages, and open fields beside the Thames — a place that feels like it’s stepped out of time.

ABOUT KELMSCOTT
Kelmscott is a small village in West Oxfordshire, sitting peacefully on the north bank of the River Thames, close to Lechlade. Its history stretches back to the Domesday Book of 1086, where it was recorded as “Chelmescote.” For centuries, it remained a rural farming settlement, surrounded by meadows and orchards that still shape its landscape today.

The village’s most famous resident was William Morris (1834–1896), the artist, poet, and leader of the **Arts and Crafts movement**. He discovered Kelmscott in 1871 and made Kelmscott Manor his summer home. The Manor, a 16th-century farmhouse built in traditional Cotswold stone, became a central source of inspiration for his work, celebrated in his writings and designs for its natural beauty and craftsmanship.

Kelmscott Manor remains one of England’s most important heritage sites, preserved by the Society of Antiquaries. It stands surrounded by traditional stone cottages, old barns, and quiet lanes that echo the rural life Morris cherished.

Today, Kelmscott is a conservation area — untouched, peaceful, and deeply atmospheric — where visitors can still sense the same rustic charm and creative inspiration that captivated William Morris more than a century ago.

title: Condicote, ENGLAND - Small English Village, Early Morning Walk
description:
Condicote is a small village located in the Cotswold district of Gloucestershire, England. It has a rich history dating back many centuries.

Like many villages in the Cotswolds, Condicote has medieval origins. It was mentioned in the Domesday Book of 1086, which was a survey of England commissioned by William the Conqueror.

The village is known for its historic manor houses, which are characteristic of the Cotswold area. These houses often date back several centuries and are built from the distinctive local honey-colored limestone.

Like much of the Cotswold region, Condicote has a history tied to agriculture. It was primarily an agricultural community, with farming being a central part of the local economy.

The village is noted for its well-preserved traditional Cotswold architecture, which includes stone cottages with steeply pitched roofs.

The Cotswold region as a whole has played a significant role in English history. Its wealth from the wool trade in the Middle Ages contributed to the construction of many of the historic buildings in the area.

title: Timeless Beauty of Tredington : Early Morning English Village WALK
description:
Join me on an early morning walk through Tredington, a charming village steeped in history. Explore picturesque thatched houses, watch locals walking their dogs, and admire beautiful plants as we uncover the village's fascinating past.

Tredington is a village rich in history, known for its numerous large farmhouses, many of which are timber-framed buildings dating back to the 16th and 17th centuries. By 1931, the village had a population of just 92 people. The centerpiece of Tredington is its ancient church, with its oldest parts built around the year 1000.

Over the centuries, the church has seen phases of construction and restoration in the 12th, 14th, 15th, and 17th or 18th centuries, with a major restoration in the 19th century. Many of Tredington’s earlier inhabitants are buried within the church, adding to the village's historical depth.

title: Painswick "Queen of the Cotswolds" WALK, || Historic Wool Town in ENGLAND
description:
Painswick's title of "Queen of the Cotswolds" is well-earned. Its Cotswold stone building-lined streets reveal true history.

Stone has been quarried from Painswick Beacon for the town buildings since Roman times. From at least the 16th Century Painswick's wool cloth industry guaranteed its prosperity.

Cloth weaving has been a fundamental part of the history of Painswick, supporting the growth in population from 118 families in 1495 to 4099 people in 1831. Initially a small scale cottage industry, later mills were powered by the fast flowing Painswick Stream.

While Royalists were encamped in Painswick, tradition has it that King Charles I went up to the Beacon and, seeing the beautiful valley to the east said "This must be Paradise". Since then that valley, and the hamlet on its western side to the north of Painswick have been called Paradise.

title: Pretty English Village - Autumn WALK || Asthall Village in the Windrush Valley
description:
Asthall has a rich history of former Roman settlement. Several later-Mesolithic and numerous Neolithic artefacts have been found in Asthall, some within areas that were woodland until 1862

The Church of England parish church of Saint Nicholas was enlarged in about 1160 and restored in 1885

Most domestic buildings in the parish are of coursed limestone rubble with stone-slated roofs, though many were originally thatched

Asthall village was also the birthplace and long time home of the actor Bob Arnold, famous as Tom Forrest in the BBC radio series 'The Archers'

In the summer of 2007 a hoard of 110 gold angel and half-angel coins was found during building work at Asthall. The coins were minted at dates from 1470 to 1526, most of them in the brief second reign of Henry VI.

Join me for a calm early morning walk through the villages of Alton Barnes and Alton Priors in Wiltshire.

Alton Barnes and Alton Priors are neighbouring villages in Wiltshire, set within the Marlborough Downs, an area known for its wide open chalk hills and ancient landscapes. The villages have early origins and appear in the Domesday Book, reflecting their long history as rural settlements.

The surrounding land has been shaped by farming for centuries, particularly sheep grazing, which contributed to the region’s agricultural heritage. The villages are closely connected to the wider prehistoric landscape, with nearby features such as long barrows and ancient earthworks scattered across the downs.

One of the most notable landmarks nearby is the White Horse carved into the hillside above Alton Barnes, a striking figure cut into the chalk and visible from across the valley. The area is also close to the Kennet & Avon Canal, which runs through the wider landscape.

With wide skies, open views, and abundant birdlife, Alton Barnes and Alton Priors offer a peaceful and expansive feel, especially in the early morning when the downs are quiet and the day is just beginning.

title: Golden Sunrise Walk | Early Morning in a Rural English Village
description:
Join me for a peaceful sunrise walk through the quiet village of Berwick Bassett, set high on the Wiltshire downs in the English Countryside. As the sun rises, soft golden light spreads across open fields, hedgerows and country lanes, creating a calm and reflective start to the day. This is a gentle, no talking walk with only natural countryside sounds.

ABOUT BERWICK BASSETT
Berwick Bassett is a small rural village in Wiltshire, located on the edge of the Marlborough Downs. Its history stretches back to at least the Domesday Book, when it was recorded as an agricultural settlement. The name “Berwick” comes from Old English, meaning outlying farm or settlement, reflecting its long farming heritage.

The village is home to St Michael’s Church, parts of which date back to the medieval period, standing quietly among fields and ancient pathways. For centuries, this area has been shaped by farming, sheep grazing and the wide open landscapes that define the downs.

Berwick Bassett sits close to ancient routes and prehistoric sites scattered across Wiltshire, adding to the timeless feeling of the landscape. At sunrise, when the light is low and the countryside is still, the village feels especially peaceful and unchanged.

title: It’s Beautiful! - Why Are You Not Here? 5 AM Summer Walk in Minster Lovell - ENGLAND
description:
Ever wondered what a Cotswold village looks like at 5 AM on a summer morning?
That’s exactly what we are exploring in Minster Lovell, tucked beside the River Windrush in Oxfordshire. With golden light, soft shadows, and almost no one around, it’s a peaceful dreamland come to life.

Minster Lovell Hall Ruins: Contains remnants of the 15th-century manor, built by William Lovell around 1440.

Ghostly Legend: Legend says the skeleton of Francis Viscount Lovell was found in a secret vault in the 1700s—and locals still claim to hear ghostly noises and see mysterious figures wandering the ruins

Thatched Cottages & Riverbank: Honey-coloured cottages and ancient stone buildings reflect beside the crystal-clear Windrush River.

St Kenelm’s Church & Village Life: The parish church was rebuilt in the 15th century. Walk with me pass traditional lanes, and pass the Old Swan Inn and Minster Mill Hotel, all part of village life that feels timeless yet full of character.

Filmed at 5 AM in early summer, this walk captures a dreamlike moment rarely seen by most.

title: The Most Photographed Cottage in the COTSWOLDS | English Village Walk on a Windy Spring Morning
description:
A windy spring morning walk through Honington, a charming English village tucked away in the Cotswolds, England. Despite the crisp wind, the beauty of spring is in full bloom — from vibrant greenery to birdsong echoing through quiet lanes.

This village is best known for Rose Cottage, one of the most photographed cottages in the Cotswolds, drawing visitors who discovered its fairytale charm through social media. But Honington is more than just picture perfect, it's a village steeped in rich English history.

Once tied to the Abbey of Evesham after the Norman Conquest, Honington has deep Anglo-Saxon roots. The grand Honington Hall, dating back to the 17th century, still stands as a symbol of the village’s aristocratic past. Honington also played a role in World War II as the site of RAF Honington, supporting bomber operations.

You’ll also pass All Saints Church, featuring a tower from the 13th century, and soak in the rural stillness that makes this village truly timeless. With a population of just around 250, it’s a wonderful snapshot of slower-paced countryside life.

Whether you're here for the stunning views, the cosy cottages, or the rich history, thank you for joining me on this quiet escape.

title: Early Morning in a English Village - Cotswold Village WALK
description:
Experience the serene beauty of North Cerney in the early morning glow. Nestled on the hillside above the River Churn in the Cotswolds, this hidden English village offers peace, history, and timeless charm.

Anglo-Saxon Origins & River Churn: The name ‘Cerney’ comes from the ancient river it overlooks, first recorded centuries ago.

Grade I‐listed All Saints’ Church: Dating back to the 12th century, complete with Norman doorways, a saddleback tower, medieval artifacts, and stunning 20th-century Gothic Revival furnishings.

Cerney House & Manor History: Once the home of the Rich and Croome families since 1660, now opening its gardens to the public,

Stunning Rural Architecture: Walk among charming stone cottages, historic barns, and a classic phone kiosk — all built from honey-colored Cotswold limestone.

Scenic Setting: Positioned within the Churn Valley’s rolling countryside, the village feels suspended in time, with around 550 residents in this tranquil parish

title: England's Countryside: A Journey Through Time in Wiltshire's Historic Village
description:
Join me on an immersive early morning walking tour of Aldbourne, a picturesque village nestled in the English Countryside in the heart of Wiltshire, England. This journey unveils Aldbourne's rich tapestry of history, from its Saxon origins—where "Aldbourne" is believed to mean "Aelda's Stream"—to its significant roles in various historical epochs.

As we wander through the village, we'll encounter the medieval Church of St. Michael, a Grade I listed building that stands as a testament to architectural evolution over the centuries. The village green, once bustling with industries like bell making, weaving, and chair making, tells tales of prosperity and resilience, especially after overcoming devastating fires in the 18th century.

Aldbourne's historical significance extends to the 20th century, serving as a base for British and Canadian forces during World War II. Notably, it hosted Easy Company of the 506th Parachute Infantry Regiment, later immortalized in the "Band of Brothers" series.

 Additionally, the village gained fame as the filming location for the 1971 "Doctor Who" story, "The Dæmons," adding a touch of sci-fi allure to its rich heritage.

This video offers a serene exploration of Aldbourne's charming streets, historic landmarks, and the stories etched into its landscape. Whether you're a history enthusiast, a "Doctor Who" fan, or simply someone who appreciates the beauty of English villages, this tour promises a captivating experience.​

title: English Countryside is the Best - Early Morning Walk in Oxfordshire
description:
If you enjoy these walks and want to support the channel, you can paypal me or join the channel membership:

Join me for a peaceful early morning walk through the village of Woolstone in Oxfordshire, nestled beneath the rolling chalk hills of the Berkshire Downs. As the day begins, the countryside is quiet, the views stretch across the landscape and the village slowly comes to life.

This walk follows quiet lanes, traditional cottages, open countryside and one of the most historic landscapes in England. With no talking or music, you can simply enjoy the natural sounds of the morning and the peaceful atmosphere of rural Oxfordshire.

Woolstone is a small historic village in Oxfordshire, situated at the foot of the Berkshire Downs and close to the famous Uffington White Horse.

The village dates back many centuries and appears in the Domesday Book of 1086. Its name is believed to derive from Old English, meaning "Wulf's settlement" or "Wulf's farm".

Woolstone's most famous neighbour is the Uffington White Horse, a prehistoric hill figure carved into the chalk hillside over 3,000 years ago during the Bronze Age. Visible for miles across the surrounding countryside, it remains one of Britain's oldest and most mysterious landmarks.

The village itself has long been associated with farming and rural life. Traditional stone cottages, quiet lanes and open fields continue to define its character today.

Surrounded by ancient landscapes, sweeping views and historic sites, Woolstone offers a glimpse of a slower pace of life in one of England's most remarkable countryside settings.

title: WALK into Spring: Exploring Ascott-under-Wychwood's Blossoming Beauty - ENGLAND
description:
Ascott-under-Wychwood is a picturesque village nestled in the Oxfordshire Cotswolds, England. Its name reflects the village's historical connection to the ancient Wychwood Forest, once a royal hunting ground.

The village has a rich history that dates back to the Domesday Book of 1086, where it is recorded as "Ascot." Over the centuries, it has evolved from a predominantly agricultural community, with its landscape marked by charming stone cottages and traditional farmhouses that echo the architectural style of the Cotswolds.

A significant historical feature in the village is the Church of the Holy Trinity, which exhibits elements from various architectural periods, including the 13th, 14th, and 15th centuries.

In the 19th century, the arrival of the Oxford, Worcester, and Wolverhampton Railway marked a turning point, contributing to local economic development but also changing the pastoral character of the village. The local railway station, originally opened in 1853, played a crucial role in connecting Ascott-under-Wychwood with larger markets and cities, although it now operates on a limited service basis.

Today, Ascott-under-Wychwood maintains a strong sense of community, upheld by local traditions and events, such as the annual village fete and various community-run projects. The village's location in the Cotswolds Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty also makes it agreat spot for walkers.

A peaceful early morning walk through the tiny village of Barton in Gloucestershire, nestled in the beautiful Windrush Valley in the heart of the Cotswolds.

Despite its small size, Barton is full of character. Quiet lanes, traditional limestone cottages, rolling countryside and the gentle sounds of rural life create a wonderfully peaceful atmosphere. With so few houses, it feels more like a hidden hamlet than a village.

There is no talking or music in this video, just natural sounds, birdsong and the calm rhythm of the English countryside.

ABOUT BARTON

Barton is a small village in Gloucestershire, located near Naunton and Temple Guiting in the Cotswolds. The village sits beside the River Windrush and has been recorded in historical documents since at least the 13th century.

What makes Barton unusual is its size. Historical records from 1779 show that the village consisted of only seven houses and forty four inhabitants, making it one of the smallest settlements in the area.

Like many Cotswold communities, Barton developed through agriculture and the wool trade, which shaped much of the surrounding landscape. Today, it remains a peaceful collection of beautiful limestone cottages surrounded by rolling countryside and the tranquil scenery of the Windrush Valley.

title: Early Morning Walk in a Small English Village - Kencot, ENGLAND
description:
Join me for a calm and peaceful early morning walk in Kencot, Oxfordshire — birdsong, fields, old stone cottages, and that tranquil countryside vibe.

Kencot is a small and very picturesque village in West Oxfordshire, about 2 miles southwest of Carterton
The parish church is St. George’s — Norman origins, with features such as the south doorway (with relief of Sagittarius shooting a monster), a tower dating to about 1300, later Perpendicular Gothic additions around 1500. It’s a Grade II* listed building.

Some old buildings: Red Rose Close (1650 by date-stone), Manor Farm House from 17th century (altered later), and Kencot House built in the early 18th century. Much of the village is inside a conservation area.

description:
Today I walk in flooded Abingdon. The Streets in Abingdon have been affected by severe flooding. There are 27 flood warnings in place across Oxfordshire at the time.

Abingdon , located in Oxfordshire, England, is a historic market town with a rich and diverse history.
Abingdon-on-Thames, as it is officially known, has ancient origins dating back to the Iron Age. It was originally a river crossing and an important settlement for the local tribe.

During the Roman era, Abingdon was a significant town named Abingdonium, boasting an important abbey and a prosperous trading center.

The town grew in prominence during the medieval period, gaining a royal charter in the 14th century and becoming an influential market town.
The market has been an integral part of Abingdon's history, serving as a hub for commerce and trade, with markets dating back centuries.

Industrial Revolution: Abingdon played a role in the Industrial Revolution, witnessing growth in industries like brewing, milling, and the manufacture of cloth.

Cultural Heritage: The town is home to several historic sites, including the remains of Abingdon Abbey, which was one of the wealthiest Benedictine monasteries in medieval England. Additionally, there are various landmarks like the County Hall Museum and the riverside walks along the Thames.

title: Zadar Croatia 4K Walk | Sunset Tour Through Old Town & Seafront
description:
Zadar Croatia unfolds slowly as the Adriatic reflects the final light. This Zadar walking tour moves through old stone streets where the city's rhythm fades into the evening. The energy changes near the waterfront—tourists wait for the Zadar sunset, locals stroll in silence.

Zadar holds a unique place in Croatia’s coastal heritage, with parts of its ancient city walls recognized by UNESCO as part of the “Venetian Works of Defence.” These fortifications, built between the 15th and 17th centuries, connect Zadar to a wider European legacy of military architecture. Today, they frame the old town’s maze of alleys, Roman ruins, and waterfront promenades making Zadar not just a tourist stop, but a link in a broader UNESCO story that defines Adriatic history.

Every step reveals more of Zadar, from Roman walls to narrow alleys filled with dusk light. A coastal route known to travelers for its open views, cool breeze, and the natural acoustics of the sea organ.

This Travel Tour captures the atmosphere of Zadar Croatia without edits, without voice. Just the real pace of the city as day closes. Perfect for travel planning, tourism research, or a quiet visual escape.

A real-time Zadar walking tour through the old town, where each turn leads to another glimpse of the coast, the churches, the sunset. No narration. Just the natural atmosphere of an evening in one of the most walked cities in Croatia.

Designed for travelers looking to explore Zadar without filters, for tourists planning a trip, and for anyone who wants to experience Zadar sunset as it unfolds. Urban, historical, coastal all in one path.

title: The England Tourists Rarely See - Early Morning Walk
description:

A peaceful early morning walk through the village of Alvescot in Oxfordshire. Unlike some of the well known Cotswold villages where tourist visit, Alvescot is a working rural village where everyday life carries on at a gentle pace.

This walk isn't about famous landmarks or postcard views. Instead, it's a chance to experience a quieter side of rural England, simple village streets, open countryside and the natural sounds that make an early morning walk so relaxing.

There is no talking or music, just birdsong, gentle countryside sounds and the peaceful atmosphere of an Oxfordshire village.

Alvescot is a small village in West Oxfordshire, located close to the Gloucestershire border and surrounded by open farmland. The village has Saxon origins and was recorded in the Domesday Book of 1086.

Its name is believed to come from Old English, meaning "Ælf's cottage" or settlement. Agriculture has shaped the village for centuries, with farming continuing to define much of the surrounding landscape today.

At the heart of the village stands St Peter's Church, whose origins date back to the 12th century, although much of the building has been altered and restored over time. Traditional limestone cottages, quiet lanes and open fields give Alvescot its understated rural character.

While Alvescot may not be one of Oxfordshire's best-known villages, it offers an authentic glimpse into everyday village life away from the busier tourist routes.

Early morning walk through the village of Whelford in the Cotswolds, where the rising sun slowly lights up the countryside and the River Coln flows quietly through the landscape.

This walk is filled with birdsong, calm water, open lakes and the gentle sounds of nature waking up for the day. As the first sunlight reaches the trees and fields, Whelford offers a wonderfully peaceful start to the morning.

There is no talking or music, just the natural sounds of birds, flowing water and the quiet beauty of the English countryside.

Whelford is a small village in Gloucestershire, close to Fairford, situated beside the River Coln in the eastern Cotswolds. The village has historic roots dating back many centuries and remains a peaceful rural community surrounded by open countryside.

The River Coln has long shaped the landscape here, providing water for agriculture and creating a rich habitat for wildlife. Today, the surrounding lakes, wetlands and riverside meadows attract a wide variety of birds throughout the year, making Whelford a popular location for nature lovers and walkers.

The village itself is made up of traditional stone cottages, quiet country lanes and open green spaces, offering a slower pace of life that has changed little over generations.

With the morning sun rising over the river and birds filling the air with song, Whelford is one of those places where nature takes centre stage.

title: Autumn English Countryside Walk and Cafe Visit for Breakfast
description:
Broad Marston & Pebworth Walk in Worcestershire – Autumn English Countryside Walk & Cosy Cafe Breakfast

Join me for a calm and relaxing autumn morning walk through the peaceful village of Broad Marston followed by a quiet breakfast at a local cafe. The video begins with the soft light of early morning, trees glowing with golden leaves and the gentle sound of footsteps through the countryside. Later, I stop at a cafe to enjoy breakfast and capture the soothing ambience of warm cups, gentle chatter, and the comfort of a slow autumn morning in rural England.

Broad Marston is a small hamlet in Worcestershire, near Honeybourne and Pebworth, part of the Vale of Evesham, an area known for its fertile farmland, historic villages, and winding country lanes. The name Marston is derived from Old English, meaning “marsh farm, reflecting the wet meadows that once surrounded the area.

Historically, Broad Marston developed as a farming settlement, with cottages and barns built from traditional red and honey toned stone. The surrounding countryside is filled with orchards, hedgerows, and open fields that are especially beautiful in autumn when the trees blaze with colour.

Just a short walk from Broad Marston lies Pebworth, a larger and very picturesque village with a history reaching back over a thousand years. It appears in the Domesday Book of 1086 as “Peberude” and has been a farming community ever since.

The village is known for its connection to William Shakespeare, who mentioned it in The Taming of the Shrew as part of “Shakespeare’s Country.” Pebworth is one of the so called “Shakespeare Villages” around Stratford-upon-Avon, celebrated for its medieval charm and half-timbered houses.

The route between Broad Marston and Pebworth is classic rural England.

title: Exploring Milton Lilbourne, ENGLAND'S Chocolate Box Village WALK - Thatched House Heaven
description:
Walking Through Milton Lilbourne, England's Chocolate Box Village which dates from 1686. Streets lined with beautiful thatched house in this beautiful, serene English village.

Milton Lilbourne is a village located in Wiltshire, England.

The area around Milton Lilbourne has been inhabited since ancient times, with evidence of Bronze Age and Iron Age settlements found nearby.

The name "Milton" suggests an Anglo-Saxon origin. Lilbourne comes from the Lilburn family who held land in the area during the Middle Ages.

Mention of Milton Lilbourne can be found in the Domesday Book of 1086, where it was recorded as "Mildentone." At that time, it was held by the Bishop of Salisbury.

The village boasts several historic buildings, including St. Peter's Church, which dates back to the 12th century. The church is known for its Norman architecture and has been designated as a Grade I listed building.

title: Is This the Most Beautiful Village in England? (5:30 AM Walk) in the English Countryside
description:
Step into the serene beauty of Buckland, a tranquil Oxfordshire village captured at dawn on 12 July 2025.

Buckland has Anglo‐Saxon roots & the Domesday Book: Buckland — meaning ‘land held by charter’ was granted to Gloucester Abbey in AD 709 and appears in the Domesday Book of 1086

St Mary’s Church is a Grade I listed building with parts dating to the 12th century, featuring stunning medieval glass once thought to be from Hailes Abbey—admired by William Morris himself.

Estate architecture & Rothschild legacy: Many cottages, the old schoolhouse, and manor buildings were influenced or built by the Rothschild family and architect George Devey in the 19th century.

Village charm: With honey‐coloured stone homes, some thatched roofs, a picturesque green, pond, and historic barn, Buckland radiates rural elegance in every corner.

Filmed just as dawn light caressed the rooftops, this walk is a tribute to peaceful mornings, hidden heritage, and English village life in its most beautiful form.

If you’re drawn to quiet beauty, historical depth, and countryside calm, this walk is for you.

title: Early Morning Summer Walk – Jacobean House & Thatched Cottages, ENGLAND
description:
Join me for a tranquil early morning summer walk through the timeless Cotswold village of Chastleton, located in Oxfordshire, England, just a short distance from Moreton-in-Marsh. Bathed in soft summer sunlight, this hidden gem offers a quiet escape into England’s historic countryside.

Chastleton House – A magnificent Jacobean mansion built between 1607–1612, one of the finest examples in England. Preserved by the National Trust, the house remained largely untouched for 400 years, giving it the feel of a genuine time capsule.

St Mary the Virgin Church – With roots dating back to the 12th century, this Grade II* listed church features Norman architecture, a 14th-century chancel, and an intimate churchyard surrounded by spring bloom.

Thatched Cottages & Cotswold Stone Homes – The village lanes have traditional thatched-roof cottages and honey-coloured limestone buildings, glowing beautifully in the dawn light.

Unspoilt Countryside – Chastleton has no shop, pub, or modern distractions — just timeless charm, history, and nature. Perfect for peaceful reflection and immersion in summers awakening.

This early walk captures the essence of rural Oxfordshire — historic, peaceful, and bathed in golden morning light.

title: Frosty And Foggy Early Morning Walk - Buscot Village | English Countryside
description:
Frosty and Foggy Early Morning Walk Misty Buscot Village | English Countryside

Buscot is a small village situated between Faringdon and Lechlade in the English Countryside. It is within short walking distance of the Thames.
The village tea shop, with a secluded garden provides lunches and teas, as well as sweets and ice creams.
Buscot Park, owned by Lord Faringdon, and run by the National Trust, is nearby.

I explore the English Countryside, brining you relaxing and calming walks around English villages and towns. I will bring you weekly videos of casual and relaxing walks around the English Countryside, sometimes beyond that. title: Bol Brac Walking Tour 4K | Croatia Summer Stroll Through Bol Croatia
description:
Walk with us in the town of Bol Croatia, sits on the southern shore of Brac Island, connected by narrow stone alleys, sea views, and open squares. This walking tour in Bol Brac moves through its streets, beaches and waterfront spots.

Bol Brac Croatia is part of the Dalmatian coast's main tourist destinations, linked by ferry to Split and known for its tight stone grid and open waterfront. The walking tour in Bol Brac runs through everyday streets and coastal paths. No overlays, no voice. Just Bol Croatia in full scale and pace.

Tourists visit Bol Croatia for beaches like Zlatni Rat o Golden Horn Beach, but the village itself reveals more in its architecture, scale, and pace. Built to match real time experience for viewers focused on Brac Island, without edits or music. Pure Bol street level observation from start to finish. This 4K walking tour in Bol Brac moves through its streets in real time, with ambient sounds recorded on location.

title: Mykonos Chora Walking Tour 4K | Mykonos Greece Streets and Atmosphere 🇬🇷
description:
Mykonos is one of the most iconic destinations in Greece, and Chora represents its heart. Walking through Mykonos Chora reveals narrow alleys, whitewashed houses, and vivid touches of blue that define the island’s unique character. This walking tour in 4K shows how daily life and timeless tradition blend in the main town of Mykonos Greece.

The walk through Mykonos Chora captures the rhythm of the town: lively squares, hidden corners, and the unmistakable Cycladic architecture. Every step in Mykonos highlights why the island has become a symbol of beauty in the Aegean. The balance between tradition and cosmopolitan life is felt in the details of its streets.

As part of the Cyclades, Mykonos holds a strong cultural identity that makes Chora much more than a tourist destination. Exploring Mykonos Greece on foot brings travelers closer to its heritage, offering an authentic view of a place that has preserved its charm through centuries.

title: Peguera Mallorca 4K Walk | Summer Streets and Seaside Promenade in Majorca
description:
Early summer light fills the streets of Peguera Mallorca, a seaside town in southwest Spain where cafés open slowly and waves break close to the promenade. The walk moves from the beach to the main avenue, showing how the rhythm of the day unfolds between sea and town.

Shaded paths, small shops, and open terraces shape the daily life of Peguera, giving the area its calm Mediterranean tone. The promenade stretches along the shore, connecting the beaches with quiet residential lanes surrounded by pine trees and holiday houses.

This 4K walking tour follows Peguera Mallorca at its own pace. Walk with no commentary, just the ambient sound and the flow of the place itself. A clear view of a Spanish coastal town where every street leads back to the sea.

#Peguera #PegueraMallorca #WalkingTour #Mallorca #Spain #4KWalk #Travel

title: Walk in Sliema at NIGHT! (Live from Malta)

description:
Join us on a walking tour through the captivating streets of Chania, Crete. Wander the winding alleys of the Chania Old Town, where Venetian and Ottoman influences merge seamlessly with modern Greek culture. Stroll along the picturesque Chania Venetian Harbor, with its iconic Chania lighthouse and bustling waterfront cafes. As we navigate through the vibrant Chania neighborhoods, you'll encounter local markets, historical landmarks, and hidden courtyards brimming with stories of Chania's rich past.

This Chania walking tour takes us through the heart of ChaniaOld Town, from the lively Municipal Market to the serene Splantzia Square. We'll visit charming shops, sample authentic Cretan delicacies, and uncover the secrets of this ancient city. Whether you’re an avid historian or simply a curious traveler, our Chania walking tour offers a unique glimpse into the daily life and heritage of Chania, Greece.

Experience Chania Crete like never before with our immersive walking tour. Perfect for solo adventurers, families, and anyone looking to delve deeper into the soul of Crete. Don't miss out on this unforgettable exploration of one of Greece's most enchanting destinations, Chania Crete.

title: English Village Autumn Sunrise Walk | Thames Lock & River at Dawn [4K Silent Walk]
description:
Join me for a peaceful early morning autumn walk through Buscot, a picturesque English village nestled along the River Thames in Oxfordshire. We'll stroll past the historic Buscot Lock as the autumn sunrise paints the water in golden hues, with only the gentle sounds of birdsong and nature to accompany us.
Buscot is a charming village with roots stretching back to Saxon times, mentioned in the Domesday Book of 1086. The village is perhaps best known for Buscot Park, an elegant 18th-century estate now owned by the National Trust, and its famous weir and lock system on the Thames. The area has long been a haven for artists and nature lovers, with its unspoiled countryside and riverside walks offering a glimpse of timeless rural England.
As we walk, you'll see misty fields dotted with grazing cows, autumn leaves carpeting the towpath, and the peaceful Thames reflecting the dawn sky. This is the English countryside at its most serene and perfect for relaxation, meditation, or simply escaping the noise of everyday life.

title: You’ll Love Langford – Early Morning English Countryside Walk in Oxfordshire, ENGLAND
description:
Join me for an early morning walk through Langford, Oxfordshire, a peaceful village full of history, timeless English countryside views, and that classic English charm.

Langford is one of Oxfordshire’s hidden gems, recorded in the Domesday Book of 1086 as a small but thriving settlement. The village is best known for St Matthew’s Church, a remarkable Grade I listed building that dates back to the late 11th century. Built from beautiful Cotswold limestone, it remains one of the finest examples of Norman architecture in the region. Inside, you’ll find a 15th-century font, medieval carvings, and fragments of rare wall paintings.

The village has long been shaped by farming and the River Thames valley, with traditional stone cottages, barns, and winding lanes giving it that unmistakable Oxfordshire countryside feel. Despite its size, Langford has played a role in the region’s story for centuries, from medieval agriculture to modern rural life.

Walking here in the quiet of the morning, with birdsong carrying across the fields and the honey-coloured stone, it feels like stepping back in time.

If you enjoy peaceful English countryside walks, historic villages, and hidden gems in England, I think you’ll love this stroll through Langford.

Welcome to a serene journey through the pristine shores of Can Picafort! A really beautiful beach in Mallorca, Spain. Enjoy the beauty of this Balearic Islands gem as we take you on a captivating Mallorca beach walk like no other in 4K resolution.

As you step onto the golden sands of Can Picafort Beach, you'll be instantly transported to a paradise where the turquoise waters of the Mediterranean meet the tranquil coastline. Join us on this exploration of nature's wonders, where every step unveils the breathtaking landscapes and vibrant atmosphere of Mallorca.

Stroll along the shoreline, feeling the soft, powdery sand beneath your feet and the gentle caress of the sea breeze. Our journey captures the essence of Can Picafort Mallorca, known for its pristine beaches, charming coastal town, and the unique fusion of Spanish and Majorca culture. Don't miss the opportunity to witness the unparalleled beauty of this Balearic jewel.

Whether you're planning a trip to Mallorca or simply craving a virtual escape to the idyllic beaches of the Balearic Islands, this beach walk in Can Picafort Mallorca is sure to captivate your senses and leave you longing for more.

Join us as we explore Mallorca Can Picafort Beach, one step at a time, and experience the magic of this Mediterranean paradise. Sit back, relax, and let the soothing waves and scenic vistas transport you to a world of serenity and beauty.

title: Exploring Paola, Malta 🇲🇹 | Walking Tour
description:
Come with me to explore Paola in Malta. This city also called Raħal Ġdid is a central-south town in Malta known for its strong local vibe, affordable rents, and excellent public transport connections, making it practical rather than pretty; it’s home to the UNESCO-listed Ħal Saflieni Hypogeum, sits close to Valletta and the Grand Harbour, and offers plenty of shops and daily services, but it’s dense, busy, and can be noisy with traffic, so it suits people who want central access and value for money rather than greenery, views, or nightlife.
Enjoy this video while we are exploring the beautiful streets of Paola.

description:

🌡️ TEMPERATURE: 14 °C

Join me for an early morning walk through Rendcomb, a beautiful old Gloucestershire village tucked into the Churn Valley near Cirencester in the Cotswolds.

The village stretches along the hillside above the River Churn, with old stone buildings, country lanes and the surrounding Cotswold landscape making it a lovely place to explore at the beginning of the day.

Rendcomb has a history stretching back more than 1,000 years. The settlement existed before the Norman Conquest and was recorded in the Domesday Book of 1086.

Over the centuries, the Rendcomb estate passed through several important families, including the de la Mares and the landscape around the village gradually developed into what became Rendcomb Park.

One of the village's historic treasures is St Peter's Church. A church has stood here since at least the 12th century, although much of the present building dates from a rebuilding in the early 16th century. Inside is an impressive Norman font that survives from the earlier church.

Above the village stands Rendcomb Park, dominated by the grand Italianate mansion designed by architect Philip Hardwick in the 19th century.

The estate later became home to Rendcomb College, founded by Frederick Noel Hamilton Wills in 1920. For more than a century, the school became an important part of life in Rendcomb before closing in July 2026.

🌡️ TEMPERATURE: 15 °C

Marston Meysey is a historic village in Gloucestershire, close to Fairford and the River Thames. The village dates back many centuries and was recorded in the Domesday Book of 1086, reflecting its long-standing place in England's rural history.

The name combines "Marston," meaning "marsh settlement" in Old English, with "Meysey," from the de Meysey family who held the manor during the medieval period. The surrounding lown lying meadows and fertile farmland have shaped village life for generations.

At the heart of the village stands St James the Great Church, parts of which date back to the 12th century. Built from local limestone, it remains a striking reminder of Marston Meysey's medieval heritage.

Today, Marston Meysey remains a quiet rural community where traditional Cotswold stone cottages, open green spaces and peaceful lanes preserve the timeless character of the English countryside. It may not be one of the region's busiest villages, but its gentle pace and authentic charm make it a rewarding place to explore on a quiet morning.

title: Early Morning Walk in a Hidden Historic Village in Oxfordshire - ENGLAND
description:
Welcome to Shutford, a tranquil village nestled in the rolling ironstone hills of north Oxfordshire, England. This video is a silent early morning walk through a community that feels frozen in time, no narration, no music, just birdsong, and the rhythm of my footsteps on lanes bordered by golden Hornton stone.

Shutford’s history stretches back centuries. Likely of Saxon origin, the name is derived from “Scytta’s Ford.” Archaeological evidence shows human activity dating to the Iron Age and Roman periods, including a large Roman settlement covering some 50 acres and nearby hillforts on Madmarston Hill.

By the medieval era, Shutford had three manors and a community of several dozen houses. In 1701 a devastating fire destroyed 24 homes, but by the late 18th century the village had recovered and grown to nearly seventy houses.

From around 1750, Shutford gained worldwide fame for its plush-weaving industry. Skilled artisans produced high-quality handwoven fabric for royal courts across Europe and even the coronation of Tsar Nicholas II in 1896.

At the heart of the village stands the 12th-century St. Martin’s Church, built in transitional Norman to Early English Gothic style. Many original features survive, including parts of the arcade and bell tower, and it has been Grade II* listed since 1955 .

The 16th-century Manor House, built by Sir Richard Fiennes, dominates a gentle rise above the village. During the English Civil War, Parliamentarian soldiers reportedly drilled in its upper hall, built before 1600. Its stone and silhouette complement the character of Shutford’s lanes.

This video captures the village green, churchyard, and quiet byways. Ideal for lovers of historic rural England, slow travel, and ambient early‐morning walks.

title: Is This England’s Perfect Countryside Village? | Early Morning COTSWOLDS WALK
description:
Welcome to Castle Eaton, a picture-perfect English village perched on the banks of the River Thames and standing like a time capsule in the English countryside. In this video, you’ll join me for an early morning walk as light breaks softly over stone cottages and the church spire —no narration, just dawn, birdsong, and some village life.

Castle Eaton has roots reaching back to the Domesday Book of 1086, when it was recorded as having around 27 households.

Over the centuries it has become known for its historic buildings built from local stone, many dating between the 1600s and 1800s, giving the village that classic Cotswold feel.

At the heart of the village stands St. Mary the Virgin Church, which features Norman doorways and a 13th-century chancel.

The striking iron girder Castle Eaton Bridge, built in 1893, spans the Thames here.
Many of the homes lie along The Street, the original main line through the village, built in local stone and preserved in a Conservation Area to protect its heritage.

 The Red Lion pub claims a special place too: it is said to be the first public house you encounter on the River Thames after its source in the Cotswolds.

This walk captures Castle Eaton at its most peaceful.

If you love old England, heritage architecture, tranquil walks, or moments when time seems to slow, this is for you. Thank you for walking with me. If this video brought you calm, beauty, or a longing to visit, please like, subscribe, and share.

Kempsford is a historic village in Gloucestershire, close to Fairford and the border with Wiltshire, lying near the upper reaches of the River Thames. Its history stretches back well over a thousand years, and it was recorded in the Domesday Book of 1086.

The village is perhaps best known for the Church of St Mary the Virgin, whose impressive tower has watched over Kempsford for centuries. Parts of the church date back to the 12th century, although much of the building was rebuilt and enlarged during the medieval period. The sound of its bells remains a familiar part of village life today.

For centuries, farming has shaped the surrounding landscape, with rich meadows along the Thames supporting agriculture and wildlife alike. The area is home to a wide variety of birds, making the early morning one of the best times to experience Kempsford at its most peaceful.

Today, Kempsford retains much of its traditional character, with quiet streets, historic cottages and a timeless rural atmosphere that reflects the gentle pace of life in this corner of the Cotswolds.

description:

🗺️ MAP: https://maps.app.goo.gl/Fj6NcJiAAwBZqzpE8
🌡️ TEMPERATURE: 14°C

A windswept early morning walk through Winstone, a small Gloucestershire village in the Cotswolds.

It has been another incredibly dry spell and the countryside is showing it. The fields have taken on their golden summer colour, while the strong morning wind moves through the grass, trees and flowers.

Along the way we meet horses and sheep grazing around the village, with plenty of beautiful summer flowers still adding colour to the landscape.

Winstone is a small historic village in Gloucestershire, situated in the Cotswolds between Cirencester and Cheltenham.

The settlement has ancient roots and was recorded in the Domesday Book of 1086. For centuries, life here was closely connected to agriculture, with the surrounding fields used for livestock and farming, a relationship with the countryside that is still very visible today.

At the heart of Winstone stands the Church of St Bartholomew. The church has medieval origins, with surviving features dating from the 11th and 12th centuries, although it was altered and restored during later centuries.

Winstone has never developed into one of the Cotswolds' busy tourist destinations. Instead, it remains a small rural community surrounded by farmland, traditional stone buildings and open countryside.

On a morning like this, with horses and sheep in the fields, flowers lining the lanes and the summer wind blowing across the landscape, it feels very much like rural England.

title: Live from Valletta on a Sunday night
Chiavari Italy | 4K Walking Tour Through the Heart of Chiavari Streets
description:
Chiavari is a Ligurian town that balances historic charm with a relaxed coastal atmosphere. This 4K walking tour moves through its central streets, showing how Chiavari Italy blends medieval arcades, lively markets, and quiet piazzas.

Located between Portofino and the Cinque Terre, Chiavari Italy is a gateway to both cultural heritage and seaside beauty. Its narrow lanes and colorful façades create a rhythm that feels both local and timeless.

Walking in Chiavari offers a close look at daily life, from the architecture of its historic center to the energy of its public squares. This video follows the route naturally, letting the city’s sounds and scenes speak for themselves.

title: 4K NYC Walking - Times Square Fall 2022 Walking Tour - Lower Manhattan Walking Tour
description:
Take a walk with me on this gorgeous day in New York City Times Square. I started walking from Bryant Park from 42nd Street on Fifth Avenue, and I went towards Times Square. No matter how often I walk in this neighborhood in Midtown Manhattan, I always get amazed by all the colorful lights in this world's busiest pedestrian area!

Did you know Times Square was formerly known as Longacre Square and was renamed in 1904 after The New York Times moved its headquarters to the newly erected Times Building.

title: Serene 7AM English Countryside Walk | Hidden Beauty in Oxfordshire - ENGLAND
description:
Join me for a peaceful early morning walk through the quiet and charming village of Littleworth in Oxfordshire, England. This unspoilt countryside gem is nestled near Faringdon and offers rolling fields, historic cottages, and a calm that only the early hours can bring.

Located just east of Faringdon, Littleworth is a small but characterful village with a deep rural charm. Known for its stone cottages, open pastures, and quintessential English village scenes, it's a perfect place to reconnect with nature.

This tranquil walk captures dew-kissed grass, birdsong, and soft golden morning light, a gentle way to start your day and take in the timeless beauty of rural England.

Whether you're watching from home or dreaming of your next countryside escape, this walk is for anyone who finds peace in nature and joy in the little details.

More about Littleworth: https://www.littleworth.org/

Through my lens, you can appreciate the beauty of the English Countryside and perhaps find inspiration for your next walk or holiday.

title: 4K NYC Walking - Columbus Circle To Fifth Ave - Walking W 59th St Along Central Park In Manhattan
description:
Take a walk with me on this energetic Saturday in Manhattan. We walk from W 57th St at 8th Ave and then pass Columbus Circle, pass W 59th St along Central Park, until we reach 5th Avenue. On the way, we will see the biggest Apple store in NYC and some other high-end stores such as Dior, Van Cleef & Arpel, Bergdorf Goodman, Louis Vuitton, BVLGARI, and Tiffany & Co. At the end of our walk, we pass the 58-floor Trump Tower!

title: On the First Day of Christmas - Rain Walk in a Traditional English Town
description:
Henley-on-Thames - Rainy Autumn Morning by the Thames & Town Christmas Lights

Join me this morning around 7:00am for a moody, christmas atmospheric walk through Henley-on-Thames, as rain falls softly and Christmas lights still glow along the streets and riverside. The Thames reflects the glow of lights, gentle ripples in the water, and wet pavements give everything a peaceful, cinematic feel, perfect for a calm, reflective stroll.

Henley-on-Thames is one of England’s most historic riverside towns, with origins dating back to the 12th century. The first known reference to Henley appears around 1179, when King Henry II is believed to have purchased land here, helping establish the town as an important river crossing and trading point.

By the 13th and 14th centuries, Henley had grown into a thriving market town thanks to its strategic position on the River Thames. It became well known for trading grain, timber, and later, goods transported along the river toward London.

The town’s famous stone bridge, the Henley Bridge, was completed in 1786. Its elegant five arches are now one of the most iconic features of the town. Nearby stands the church of St Mary the Virgin, whose striking tower dominates the skyline and has been part of the riverside view since medieval times.

In the 19th century, Henley became internationally recognised for rowing, hosting the first Henley Royal Regatta in 1839. This annual event transformed the town into a centre for rowing culture, drawing competitors and visitors from around the world.

Despite its long history, Henley has retained much of its traditional charm winding streets, Georgian frontages, old inns, quaint shops, and an active riverside. During winter, especially around Christmas, the town glows with lights and festive decorations, creating a warm and atmospheric setting along the Thames.

Join me as we explore the timeless beauty, ancient past, and tranquil countryside of this hidden gem in England. A perfect escape into history and nature

title: Step Back in Time: Walking Through the Ancient Village of Avebury
description:
Step back in time as I take you on a serene walk through the historic village of Avebury, surrounded by one of the largest Neolithic stone circles in the world. Captured on a crisp winter’s day, this peaceful walk offers a glimpse of the beauty and mystery of this ancient site.

With stones dating back over 4,500 years and a rich history of preservation and discovery, Avebury is a must-visit for history enthusiasts and countryside lovers alike. Enjoy the charm of this picturesque village, its tranquil atmosphere, and the freedom to wander among the stones—a unique experience unlike Stonehenge.

Avebury's stone circle is significantly larger than Stonehenge, both in terms of the size of the circle and the number of stones. The stone circle itself originally had around 100 stones, though many have been removed or fallen over time. The site also includes two smaller stone circles and the remnants of a complex of Neolithic structures.

Sit back, relax, and immerse yourself in the breathtaking beauty of Avebury’s ancient landscape.

title: Walking 57th Street NYC: Billionaires’ Row to the East Side | 4K NYC Walk
description:
#NYCWalk #BillionairesRow #57thStreet #4KCityWalk #manhattanvibes

Take a full walk across 57th Street in Manhattan — from 8th Avenue all the way to 3rd Avenue. This route passes through one of NYC’s most iconic and contrasting streets: from the luxury of Billionaires’ Row to the vibrant, everyday life of the East Side. Along the way, you’ll see towering skyscrapers, local shops, city traffic, and a real slice of New York energy. Filmed in 4K for a full immersive experience.
No talking, just city sounds and atmosphere

🎥 Filmed on: 4:00 PM Friday, May 23, 2025

title: Early Morning WALK Through Real-Life Storybook Villages! ENGLAND
description:
Join me on a tranquil early morning walk through Broughton Poggs and Little Faringdon in Oxfordshire. Horses grazing, chickens clucking, golden light across fields — this is the English countryside magic.

**Broughton Poggs**
Part of the civil parish of Filkins & Broughton Poggs, in West Oxfordshire.
The parish church (St Peter’s) has Norman roots from the 12th century, with additions over the ages.
Broughton Hall, originally built in the 16th century, has been altered through the 17th-18th centuries.

**Little Faringdon**
- A tiny historic estate village with origins going back to the Anglo-Saxon/Medieval period.
- Manor once held by Beaulieu Abbey; church of St Margaret’s has Norman structure and later Gothic

If you enjoy this walk — hit **Like**, **Hype**, and leave a comment telling me your favourite moment. Every bit helps this video reach more people who love peaceful countryside vibes.

title: Corfu Walking Tour | Explore Corfu Town, Corfu Greece in 4K
description:
Join us on a comprehensive Corfu walking tour through the historic streets of Corfu Town in Corfu island Greece. Walkig discover the blend of Venetian, French, and British influences in this UNESCO World Heritage site. In this tour, we explore key landmarks such as the Old Fortress, Liston promenade, and the Church of Agios Spyridon. Perfect town for travelers planning a visit to Corfu Greece or for virtual tourists interested in Corfu City.

Corfu Town also known as Kerkyra offers a delightful blend of Greek, Venetian, and French influences, creating a unique and picturesque ambiance. Stroll along the Esplanade, visit the famous Liston promenade, and soak up the breathtaking views of the Ionian Sea. Our walking tour Corfu Old Town will guide you through the must-visit spots in Corfu Greece and provide insider tips to make the most of your time in this enchanting Corfu Town Greece Cultural UNESCO World Heritage Site.

title: La Spezia Walking Tour 4K Italy Summer Streets and Harbor
description:
La Spezia opens onto the Liguria Sea with streets that lead from the city center to the harbor. This is where the rhythm of daily life meets the calm of a coastal town. The walk captures how La Spezia moves between quiet alleys, wide boulevards, and waterfront views.

La Spezia is also the main gateway to Cinque Terre, with daily trains and ferries connecting the city to the five villages. Its location makes La Spezia a natural starting point for travelers exploring this part of Italy.

Walking in La Spezia Italy shows the connection between the city’s maritime character and its traditional streets. This 4K walk brings out the natural sounds and details of the city without narration. It’s a simple way to see La Spezia as it is in motion, under summer light.

La Spezia Italy keeps its own pace, between the sea and the hills. A walk here feels both relaxed and full of life.

Calmsden is a small hamlet in the parish of North Cerney, just north of Cirencester, within the Cotswolds National Landscape. Although tiny, it has a long rural history and is surrounded by farmland that has shaped the area for centuries.

The hamlet is home to St Mary's Church, parts of which date back to the 12th century, and several traditional limestone cottages that reflect the classic architecture of the Cotswolds.

Historically, Calmsden has always been closely linked to agriculture. The surrounding estate and farmland remain an important part of village life today, with arable farming and conservation shaping much of the landscape.

Although small, Calmsden captures everything many people love about the Cotswolds—quiet lanes, honey-coloured stone buildings, rolling countryside and the peaceful rhythm of rural England.

title: Naples, Italy 4K Walking Tour 🇮🇹
description:
Welcome to Naples, Italy! In this walking tour we take you on a detailed tour through Naples and its streets rich in history, culture, and stunning architecture. Our Naples walking tour showcases the city’s rich artistic heritage, from ancient ruins to Baroque masterpieces. Explore the local atmosphere, soak in the stunning views, and experience the unique blend of history and modern Naples life.

This Naples Walking Tour takes you on a captivating journey, unveiling iconic landmarks and Naples local atmosphere. Each step reveals the essence of Naples, showcasing the unique character of the Historic Centre of Naples, a designated UNESCO World Heritage Site in Italy.

During this tour, we'll visit Naples historical landmarks such as Murales Maradona 1990 Napoli, Chiesa di San Domenico Maggiore, and the vibrant Galleria Umberto I. Experience the unique charm of Naples Italy as we wander through its bustling streets, smell delicious pizzas, and uncover the stories behind its most famous sites.

title: Lugano Switzerland Walking Tour 4K | Sunday Walk in Lugano
description:
Lugano is one of the most vibrant cities in southern Switzerland, known for its lakeside charm and lively streets. This Lugano walking tour in 4K shows the rhythm of the city on a Sunday, when locals and visitors enjoy the relaxed atmosphere of the historic center and open squares.

Lugano Switzerland blends Italian influence with Swiss elegance, making it unique in architecture, food culture, and daily life. Exploring Lugano on foot highlights the way the city opens toward Lake Lugano while keeping its character in the narrow streets and elegant arcades.

As part of the Ticino region, Lugano has become a reference point for travelers who want both culture and nature in one place. This Lugano Switzerland tour captures how the city connects its lakeside setting with urban life, creating one of the most attractive destinations in the country.

Walking through Lugano on a Sunday reflects the balance of leisure and tradition. Cafés, markets, and waterfront views come together naturally, making Lugano one of the highlights of Switzerland to experience step by step.

Join me for an immersive 4K walking tour through Gamla Stan, the breathtaking Old Town of Stockholm, Sweden. In this walk, we explore the winding cobblestone alleys, vibrant historic squares, and hidden gems that make this one of the most beautiful medieval city centers in Europe. Experience the unique atmosphere of Stockholm’s historic heart like never before, from the Royal Palace to the narrowest streets in the city.

title: The Perfect Morning Walk || Lechlade Town, English Countryside
description:
The historic small town of Lechlade sits in an Area of Natural Beauty on the River Thames, with good road links from all directions and within easy reach of all the Cotswold villages and English countryside.
Lechlade sits along the River Thames and gets its name from the River Leach which joins the Thames just east of the town.

Lechlade played an important part in the Cotswold Wool trade and is mentioned in the Doomsday book. The building of the Church started in about 1472 and was completed in 1476.


About My Channel:
I explore the English Countryside, brining you relaxing and calming walks around English villages and towns. I will bring you weekly videos of casual and relaxing walks around the English Countryside, sometimes beyond that. My videos help you to relax and find peace in the ambience of nature, no added music, no talking, just walking and exploring the beauty of the English Countryside through my lens. You may even find inspiration for your next walk or holiday.

#4kwalk #stockholmwalk #swedenwalk #stockholm #sweden #gamlastan #oldtown

Hey there, my wonderful friends! 💕 Join me on a captivating 4K walk through Gamla Stan, Stockholm's enchanting Old Town. As we explore this historic gem together, you'll be immersed in its rich history and vibrant atmosphere. From charming cobblestone streets to iconic landmarks. So, sit back, relax, and let's embark on exploration of Gamla Stan. Don't forget to check out the timestamps below for quick navigation:

Thank you for joining me, and I hope you thoroughly enjoy our walk through this incredible piece of Stockholm's history and culture. 💕

title: Olbia Walking Tour 4K | Travel arround Sardinia Italy
description:
Join us for a walking tour through Olbia, Sardinia and explore this vibrant Mediterranean city full of history, culture, and charm. Located on the northeastern coast of Sardinia, Olbia is a perfect blend of ancient heritage and modern life, offering visitors a unique perspective of the island.

This 4K walking tour takes you through Olbia key attractions, including historical landmarks like the Church of San Simplicio and the Archaeological Museum, revealing the rich Roman and pre-Roman past that shaped the city. As we stroll along the lively streets and peaceful squares of Olbia, you’ll get a true feel for the local culture and the beauty of Sardinia city life.

Whether you’re planning travel or curious about Olbia Sardinia, this travel video provides a comprehensive look at Olbia's most important sights. From the iconic Corso Umberto to the serene views of the Gulf of Olbia, every step reveals something special about this charming city.

Experience the best of Olbia, Sardinia and see why it’s a must visit destination in the Mediterranean.

description:
Discover the beauty of Oristano, Sardinia, on this 4K walking tour through the city's most iconic sites. From the medieval Tower of St. Christophoros to the magnificent St. Mary’s Cathedral, each step offers a glimpse into Oristano’s rich history and cultural heritage. Wander through its quaint piazzas and vibrant local markets, where the essence of Sardinian life unfolds. Whether you're a history enthusiast or simply looking for a picturesque destination, Oristano’s captivating blend of old-world charm and modern vitality will leave you inspired. Join us as we uncover the treasures of Oristano in the heart of Sardinia.

In this walking tour, you'll get an up close look at Oristano breathtaking beauty and historical landmarks, all captured in stunning detail. Perfect for travelers and tourists planning their next trip to Sardegna, this video offers a virtual journey to one of most scenic locations in Sardinia. Whether you're preparing for a visit or simply dreaming of your next adventure, this walking tour provides an unforgettable experience of Oristano’s charm and culture.

title: Monterosso al Mare Walking Tour 4K | Monterosso Italy
description:
Monterosso al Mare walking tour 4K on Italy's Ligurian coast. This Monterosso Italy walking tour follows the beach promenade, old town center and seafront paths with natural ambient sound.

The Monterosso walking tour connects the historic village to the wide sandy beach through a tunnel carved in rock. Monterosso al Mare waterfront, Neptune statue and coastal squares complete this seaside experience.

Located in the Cinque Terre region, Monterosso offers the only extensive beach among the coastal villages. Its open shoreline and relaxed rhythm set it apart on the Italian Riviera.

00:00 Beach promenade
02:15 Old town center
05:30 Tunnel passage
08:45 Seafront cafes
12:20 Neptune statue
16:00 Village squares

Monterosso al Mare walking tour in 4K with authentic coastal atmosphere and no commentary.

title: What Sunday Feels Like in NYC: From Hudson to SoHo | 4K Walk
description:
#nyc #4kwalk #NYCwalk #4KwalkingTour #SoHoNYC
Join me on this relaxing 4K walk through New York City’s West Side, starting from the streets of Hudson Street and Bleecker Street and heading toward the energetic vibe of SoHo on a sunny Sunday. Experience the contrast between calmer residential areas and the weekend buzz of downtown Manhattan.

In this 4K NYC walking tour, you’ll see charming brownstones, cozy cafes, weekend street scenes, and stylish SoHo corners packed with life. Whether you're exploring virtually or planning your own trip to New York City, this walking tour in 4K captures the real vibe of NYC’s West Village, Bleecker Street, and SoHo on a Sunday afternoon.

🎥 Filmed on: 4:15 PM Sunday, May 25, 2025

title: 4k Stockholm Walk Stockholm Bright Summer 2024
description:
Join me on a 4K walk through the vibrant heart of Stockholm’s Södermalm, starting at the lively Swedenborgsgatan and weaving your way through Medborgarplatsen, Götgatan, and Slussen before ending in the enchanting Gamla Stan, Stockholm’s Old Town. This evening stroll captures the essence of Stockholm’s nightlife, passing by bustling bars, cozy restaurants, and lively streets filled with people enjoying happy hour. Experience the unique atmosphere of Södermalm as the sun sets and the city comes alive with energy, showcasing the perfect blend of historic charm and modern vibrancy.

title: Blenheim Palace Walk: Discovering England's Biggest House & the Birthplace of Churchill
description:
Blenheim Palace is in the pretty town of Woodstock, Oxfordshire and has been called "the finest view in England", offering a fascinating glimpse of British history.

The palac is one of England's largest houses and was built between 1705 and 1722 , designed by Sir John Vanbrugh.

Blenheim Palace sits at the edge of the picturesque town of Woodstock in Oxfordshire and is only a twenty-minute journey from the city of Oxford.

Blenheim Palace is home to the 12th Duke and Duchess of Marlborough and it was at Blenheim Palace on the 30th November 1874 at 1.30am that Winston Churchill was born.

Blenheim Palace was a gift from a grateful Queen Anne to John Churchill.

Blenheim Palace is one of the largest and most accomplished aristocratic country residences in England.

More on Blenheim palace in the link below:
https://www.british-history.ac.uk/vch/oxon/vol12/pp448-460

POSTCODE: OX20

title: Shiraz 4K Walk | Explore the REAL Iran: Shiraz Part I ایران شیراز
description:
Join me on this adventurous journey through the vibrant streets of Iran, as we explore the reality of this country versus how it is often portrayed in the media. From the bustling Vakil Bazaar, filled with colorful spices and handcrafted goods, to the serene Nasir-ol-Molk Mosque with its mesmerizing stained glass windows, this video takes you beyond the typical tourist path. Discover the rich culture, history, and daily life of one of Iran’s most captivating cities. Stay tuned for Part II of this series, where we dive deeper into the wonders of Iran, showcasing places and stories that reveal a different side of this mysterious country. Don't forget to like, subscribe, and hit the notification bell to join me on this adventure!

description:
#NYCWalk #Manhattan #4KWalkingTour #NYCFerry #SouthStreetSeaport #LowerManhattan

Take a different path into New York City.
In this 4K walking tour, we start with a peaceful ferry ride from Queens across the East River, arriving at Pier 11 in Lower Manhattan. From there, we explore a lesser-known side of the city — quiet waterfront piers, historic streets, and hidden corners near the Seaport District and Fulton Street.

title: 4K NYC Walking - 2022 Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade
description:
Hey Friends! Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade is an annual parade in New York City presented by the department store chain Macy's. The Parade is the second-oldest Thanksgiving parade in the United States. It first took place in 1924 and continued till this year. However, the Parade was canceled three years in a row during World War II.

Lining for getting an excellent place to watch the Parade usually starts around 6 AM or even earlier. Yesterday I heard some people were waiting on the street even from 4 AM. Early comers typically bring their own chairs and blankets to make the waiting easier, but it is not easy to find a good spot. However, if you live in NYC or plan to visit NYC on thanksgiving day, I highly recommend going and watching in person. It is lots of fun.
Today, we will watch the Parade from E 56th St!


About Me 👩
I'm Ellie, a tech girl living in New York City who loves to walk, discover new places and film!

title: "Award Winning Beach" Mistaken For The "CARIBBEAN" || Rhossili Bay Beach Walk - Wales
description:
Picturesque lush green surroundings, wide array of birds and ponies to be found, sandy beach and some photoworthy backdrops, noted on my visit to Wales.

Today I am in worms head, Rhossili Bay in Swansea, Wales, is named number one beach in the UK and Europe. It even made the top 10 in the World beating Hawaii and the Caribbean!

The Gower coast has strong maritime ties and a number of legends surrounding seafaring, smuggling, and piracy. Rhossili is part of the Gower Coast National Nature Reserve.

Rhossili Bay, the largest expanse of white sand on Gower, stretches for three miles to the islet of Burry Holms. The tidal island of Worm's Head is located at he southern end of the beach,

The bay has been used as the setting of New Earth in the sci-fi show Doctor Who.

Facilities available in the area:
*Pub in Rhossili village
*Restaurant/cafe in Rhossili village
*Surf hire in Rhossili village
*National Trust Visitor Centre and Shop in Rhossili
*Public toilets (adjacent to NT Visitor Centre and Shop) in Rhossili
*Coastguards (at Coastguard Lookout)

There is a steep path that leads down the side of the cliff, down to the beach, but as you head back up, you may find the path challenging to climb back up to the car park. For spectacular panoramic views over the bay put "worms head" if using a satnav which will take you to the most spectacular views.


About My Channel:
I explore the English Countryside, brining you relaxing and calming walks around English villages and towns. I will bring you weekly videos of casual and relaxing walks around the English Countryside, sometimes beyond that. My videos help you to relax and find peace in the ambience of nature, no added music, no talking, just walking and exploring the beauty of the English Countryside through my lens. You may even find inspiration for your next walk or holiday.


DATE RECORDED : APRIL 2022

title: Walk with me from Valletta to Sliema at night
4K NYC Walk | Brooklyn Charming Streets & Brownstones
description:
#brooklyn #nycwalkingtour #parkslope #nycwalk

Park Slope Brooklyn Walking Tour New York City. Brooklyn Charming Streets & Brownstones.
Park Slope, a neighborhood in Brooklyn, NYC, is known for its charming, tree-lined streets, historic brownstone buildings, and a family-friendly atmosphere. It's a vibrant, diverse area that offers a mix of cultural attractions, boutique shops, and trendy restaurants. Park Slope is also home to Prospect Park, a vast green space designed by the same architects who created Central Park. The neighborhood is popular for its strong sense of community, excellent schools, and relaxed, yet lively vibe. It's also known for its progressive values and walkable streets, making it a favorite for both families and young professionals.

🎥 Filmed on: 3:50 PM Saturday, October 19, 2024
 Temperature: 71°F | 21°C 🌤️

I'm Ellie, a tech girl living in New York City who loves to walk, discover new places and film!

Pompeii 4K Walking Tour Captivating Ancient Ruins Italy 🇮🇹
description:
Walk with us in Pompeii, Italy! Embark on a 4K walking tour through Italy ancient ruins of Pompeii frozen in time by Mount Vesuvius's AD 79 eruption. Pompeii as UNESCO World Heritage Sites, these Roman remains stand as Italy prized attractions. Our hour-long Pompeii walking tour melds archaeological wonders with an perfect summer day.

Pompeii stands as an unparalleled archaeological gem, inviting you to decipher history's enigma. Our Ruins of Pompeii walking tour video mesmerizes with intricate frescoes and structures in 4K. High-definition clarity revives Pompeii history, letting you virtually stroll its streets.

title: 4K NYC Walk - Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade 2023
description:
#macysthanksgivingdayparade #thanksgivingday #nycwalk #4kwalkMacy's
Thanksgiving Day Parade is an annual parade in New York City presented by the department store chain Macy's. The Parade is the second-oldest Thanksgiving parade in the United States. It first took place in 1924 and continued till this year. However, the Parade was canceled three years in a row during World War II.

Lining for getting an excellent place to watch the Parade usually starts around 6 AM or even earlier. Early comers typically bring their own chairs and blankets to make the waiting easier, but it is not easy to find a good spot. However, if you live in NYC or plan to visit NYC on thanksgiving day, I highly recommend going and watching in person. It is lots of fun.
Today, we will watch the Parade from E 56th St!

🎥 Filmed on: 9:00 AM Thursday, Nov 23, 2023
Temperature: 43°F| 6°C 🌤️


About Me 👩
I'm Ellie, a tech girl living in New York City who loves to walk, discover new places and film!

If you like this video, please give it a thumbs up and subscribe to my channel for more videos ❤️

Follow me on Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/ellie.walkss

title: ✨🗽 4K NYC Christmas Walk - Bryant Park Winter Village 2022 Holiday Market & Ice Skating
description:
Hey friends! We are getting closer to the holiday season, and the holiday vibe is getting stronger in New York City. Today we will walk at Winter Village's charming holiday market at Bryant Park. We are going to take a close-up look at the holiday shops! Also, watch the ice skating in the heart of the park.

I'm forever grateful that you're here! ❤️ If you like this video, please give it a thumbs up and subscribe to my channel for more videos.

About Me 👩
I'm Ellie, a tech girl living in New York City who loves to walk, discover new places and film!
